title: The Great Depression
description: Severe economic downturn caused by the 1929 stock market crash, banking panics, and tight monetary contraction. US GDP fell ~27% over 4 years.

references.name: Monetary History of the United States

title: 1973 OPEC Oil Embargo Recessions
description: OPEC oil embargo quadrupled petroleum prices, triggering global stagflation (simultaneous inflation and economic contraction) across industrial economies.

references.name: NBER Business Cycle Expansions and Contractions

title: 1981–1982 Volcker Anti-Inflation Recessions
description: Federal Reserve Chairman Paul Volcker raised the Fed Funds rate to 20% to break double-digit US inflation, leading to a sharp recession followed by long-term disinflation.

title: 1990–1991 Early 1990s Recessions
description: Short recession associated with oil price spikes during the Gulf War and commercial real estate headwinds.

title: 2001 Post-Dotcom Recessions
description: Mild US recession triggered by the collapse of technology equity valuations and compound shock of the September 11 attacks.

references.name: US Bureau of Economic Analysis Historical GDP

title: 2008 Great Recession
description: Severe global economic downturn precipitated by the subprime mortgage crisis, Lehman Brothers collapse, and global credit crunch. World GDP contracted for the first time post-WWII.

title: 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic Recession
description: Sharpest, shortest economic contraction in modern history caused by global public health lockdowns, followed by unprecedented monetary and fiscal stimulus.
